sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Capacity Management is the unified scope-driven workspace introduced in v5.2 that replaced the legacy My Team / Organization Overview tabs. The **Workspace** at `/capacity` is the home page: a person-centric stacked-bar timeline driven by a **Scope Bar** (persona-default scope plus All-CCs / per-Location / per-hierarchy-node / My-CC pills), a 5-card KPI summary, smart filter chips with live count badges, a sticky-bottom demand-vs-supply strip, and side-panel drill-downs for people / cells / projects. CC Owners triage through a dedicated **Resource Requests** inbox at `/capacity/requests`. A chronological audit trail lives at `/capacity/history`. Project Leads see a privacy-preserving **Resource Availability** view at `/capacity/availability` and can also open it as a 50%-viewport slide-over from the Project Workbench (v5.2 W6, see Workbench → Check Availability section).

sections.title: Scope Bar & Personas
sections.body: The Scope Bar at the top of `/capacity` lets you switch the workspace between **All CCs**, a single **Location** (Munich / Pune / Stuttgart), a single **Hierarchy node** (e.g. Truck & Bus Systems / Application Development), or **My CC** (the current CC for CC Owners; not visible to Executives). Persona defaults: Controller and Executive land at All CCs; CC Owner lands at My CC; Project Lead is redirected to `/capacity/availability` per spec §15. The **Capacity Dashboard** layer (four chart cards) only renders when scope spans more than one CC — narrowing to My CC slides it away. Scope changes are reflected in the URL (`?scope=…&cc=…`) so views are bookmarkable.

sections.title: Workspace Timeline
sections.body: The timeline renders one row per person grouped by role; columns are months with a collapsible year/quarter axis. Project allocations stack as colored segments per spec §3 — each project gets a stable color from a 12-color palette assigned at workspace mount. **Over-allocation** is signalled by a red border on segments where the person's monthly hours exceed 100% of standard. Clicking a person row opens a 280px side panel (`PersonDetail`) with the person's allocations, monthly utilization summary, and any pending resource-request cards with a `Review project` CTA. Clicking a cell opens `CellDetail` with that month's role context and pending-demand context. Switch to **group-by-project view** (§10) via the toggle above the timeline — rows then cluster under each project group with assigned-people rows + unassigned-slot rows + external-cost rows + a sticky-bottom unassigned summary.

sections.title: KPI Summary Bar & Filter Chips
sections.body: Five KPI cards above the timeline: **Headcount** (people in scope), **Avg utilization** (weighted across visible window), **Over-allocated** (count of person-months > 100%), **Pending requests** (count of pending RRs in scope; reads from the inbox endpoint, falls back to `—` for Executive who can't reach the inbox per §12.1), and **Supply gap** (sum of unfulfilled-demand hours). Below the KPIs, **filter chips** (`All` / `Over-allocated` / `Under-utilized` / `Pending requests` / `Unassigned months`) toggle the timeline's row filter. Each chip shows a live count badge in person view; in project-group view the chip vocabulary swaps to project-level predicates (drops `Unassigned months` merged into `Pending requests`, adds **`Needs staffing`**) and the badge counts are computed against project records instead of person rows. Chips use `aria-pressed` for screen-reader announcement of the active state.

sections.title: Demand-vs-Supply Strip
sections.body: A sticky-bottom demand-vs-supply strip (per spec §8) shows unfulfilled-request pressure per visible period. Cells are color-coded by the hours-gap between unfulfilled demand and available supply: green when supply ≥ demand, amber when 1–200h short, red when 200+h short. Clicking a cell opens a side panel listing the pending resource requests for that period; each row carries a `Review project` CTA into the assignment panel. The strip hides entirely when no period in scope carries pending demand (v5.2 W6 polish per §8.5).

sections.title: Capacity Dashboard (multi-CC scope)
sections.body:
Visible to Controller and Executive only when scope is multi-CC (All CCs / Location / Hierarchy node). Four cards in a 2×2 grid above the timeline (collapsible per-user, state persisted in localStorage):

- **Utilization distribution** — a six-bucket histogram (0%, 1–25%, 26–50%, 51–75%, 76–100%, >100%) of the people in scope. Clicking a bucket activates the matching filter chip on the timeline below (v5.2 W4 + W6 wiring): `>100%` → Over-allocated; `0%` / `1–25%` → Under-utilized; other buckets → no filter (visual highlight only).
- **Capacity forecast** — a time-series of available / allocated / demand hours over the visible window with a green-surplus / red-deficit gap shading. Clicking a month bar auto-expands the containing quarter and scrolls the timeline below to that column (v5.2 W6 §11.4 wiring).
- **Headcount breakdown** — a stacked bar switchable across Location / Hierarchy / Role / Cost Centre. Clicking a segment pushes a scope change for the segment's entity (Location → workspace scope = Location; CC → scope = My CC + that CC pinned). Role segments don't change scope (roles aren't a scope dimension).
- **Hotspot list** — top-5 hotspots ranked by severity across over-allocation, unfulfilled-demand, and chronic under-utilization. Clicking a row opens the side panel with the relevant detail (PersonDetail for over/under-utilization rows, CellDetail for unfulfilled-demand rows).

sections.title: Resource Requests Inbox
sections.body:
At `/capacity/requests` — the project-per-CC triage table for CC Owners (and Controllers, who see all CCs; Executives have read-only access via the workspace KPIs only). Each row groups all of a project's resource requests directed at one CC, with role badges, total unassigned hours, age, priority, and status (`new` / `in-progress` / `re-confirm`). CR-triggered re-confirmations carry a distinct blue pill. Clicking **Review & Assign** opens the assignment panel for that project (deep-links via `/capacity?assignment_project=…&cc=…`).

A collapsible **Recently completed** section at the bottom surfaces your CC's actions over the last 7 days with action-type badges (Confirmed / Partial / Declined / Declined request / Re-confirmed). Rows are non-actionable; a **View full history** link opens the audit trail page.

sections.title: Assignment Panel
sections.body:
Opens at 400px width on top of the workspace via deep-link `?assignment_project=<id>&cc=<id>` (or via the inbox / person-detail / demand-strip / project-view entry points described in the Timeline Ghost Overlay section below). Header carries the project name, hierarchy node, and PL. The **completion progress** bar above the role sections renders as `N full · N partial · N unassigned` per spec §9.5; the bar turns green only on full coverage at requested hours, amber when every month has at least one person but some are partial, otherwise blue.

Below the header, requests are grouped by **role section** (collapsible, with quick-fill bulk assignment). Each role section lists per-month rows. Each month row shows the requested hours, any current chip(s) (one chip per assigned person), an **[Assign]** button when empty, and a **[+ Add]** button when partial (see Multi-Person Month Splits below). Clicking [Assign] or a chip opens the **person picker** — candidates are grouped by `Matching role` first, then `Other roles`; each candidate shows their projected utilization for that month, color-coded green / amber / red.

The action bar at the bottom of the panel offers **Save Draft** (writes one `assign_draft` audit log line), **Confirm** / **Confirm partial & send to controller** (writes `confirm` or `partial_confirm` per the per-month sum check), or **Decline** with required reason (writes `decline` for the whole project).

sections.title: CR Re-Confirmations
sections.body: When a project's CR has been routed to your CC for re-confirmation, the assignment panel renders inline diffs at the role section level: **blue** badges + bars for months whose hours **increased**, **orange** for months that **decreased**, and `unchanged` rows pre-fill with the existing assignment so you don't have to redo them. The action bar's `Confirm` writes `cr_reconfirm` rather than `confirm` — except when the per-month sum check finds partial months, in which case `partial_confirm` takes precedence (the controller history filter for `Partial` is the more actionable signal). The CR id and CR direction are preserved in the audit row's `cr_id` column and `detail_payload` for the §12.13 history-detail expansion.

sections.title: Multi-Person Month Splits (v5.2 W5)
sections.body:
A single resource request month can be fulfilled by multiple people, each contributing a portion of the requested hours. On any month row that already has an assignment, click **+ Add** to open a person picker with an editable hours input pre-filled with the remaining hours. Pick a second person and the row shows two chips with their individual portions, e.g. `F. Keller 40h (72%)` and `L. Fischer 40h (45%)`.

**Hours sum to the request total.** When you type a value larger than what's left, the largest existing share is reduced automatically so the sum stays at the requested hours. Otherwise the new person is appended without touching existing chips. Removing one chip leaves the other(s) intact; removing the last chip clears the row.

**Partial assignments are allowed.** A month where the per-person sum is less than the requested hours shows a `Nh remaining` indicator. The progress bar above the role sections breaks the count down as `N full · N partial · N unassigned`, and the action bar offers **Confirm partial & send to controller** when any month is partially assigned. The controller is notified of the partial fulfillment in their approval review.

sections.title: Recently Completed & Audit Trail (v5.2)
sections.body:
The Resource Requests inbox (`/capacity/requests`) ends with a collapsible **Recently completed** section showing your CC's actions over the last 7 days — confirms, partials, declines, and CR re-confirmations. Rows are non-actionable and link to the project workspace in read-only mode. A **View full history** link at the bottom opens the audit trail page.

The full audit trail at `/capacity/history` lists every capacity action chronologically with filters for acting user, action type, cost centre, project, and date range. Click any row's chevron to expand the structured detail payload — roles affected, people assigned, partial-month counts, decline reason. Action types include `confirm`, `partial_confirm` (logged automatically when a project is confirmed with one or more partially-assigned months), `decline`, `decline_request` (single-request decline within the assignment panel), `assign_draft`, and `cr_reconfirm` for change-request re-confirmations.

sections.title: Timeline Ghost Overlay & Click-to-Assign (v5.2 W5)
sections.body:
While the assignment panel is open, the person-centric timeline switches into **assignment mode**: dashed-border *ghost segments* in the active project's color appear on each candidate person's bar for the months that resource request covers.

**Visual cues:**
- *Matching role* candidates (whose role matches the request's role) get 30% opacity and a 1.5px dashed border. *Other roles* get 15% opacity and a 1px dashed border so they're visible as fallback candidates without dominating the view.
- A **red dashed border** previews over-allocation — adding the request's hours to the person's existing allocation would push them past 100% in that month.
- During CR re-confirmations the border switches to **blue** for increased months and **orange** for decreased months, matching the in-panel diff legend.
- Role groups that contain matching candidates auto-expand the moment assignment mode is entered, so you don't need to drill in manually.

**Gestures (§9.6):**
- *Click a ghost segment* — assigns that person to that month for the full remaining hours. The block flips to a solid (just-assigned) state and the panel's progress bar updates live.
- *Click a solid just-assigned segment* — undoes the gesture; the block reverts to a ghost.
- For collapsed-period (quarter or year) cells the click acts on the first month inside the period; expand the period to operate at month granularity.

**Entry points (verified end-to-end in v5.2 W6):**
- The Resource Requests inbox `Review & assign` button (deep-link via `?assignment_project=…&cc=…`).
- The person-detail panel's `Review project` button on a pending-request card.
- A click on a yellow / red **Unfulfilled** strip cell beneath the timeline opens a side panel listing the pending projects in scope, each with its own `Review project` button.
- An italic **unassigned-slot row** in group-by-project view (clicking it routes to the assignment panel pre-scrolled to the relevant role section).
- Direct URL navigation via `?assignment_project=<pid>&cc=<ccId>`.
- The legacy `/capacity/project-assignment/<pid>` deprecation redirect (preserves any `cc` / `cr` query params and pins `scope=my_cc` so external bookmarks land cleanly inside the workspace, v5.2 W6 fix).

sections.title: PL Resource Availability (v5.2 W4)
sections.body: Project Leads are redirected from `/capacity` to `/capacity/availability` — a privacy-preserving role-and-location grid. Each cell shows two-layer fill (allocated / available hours per role × month), a `⚡N` competing-demand badge when more than one PL has a pending request for that role/location/period, a monthly breakdown side panel on click, and a location-comparison panel. A **Request this role** CTA opens the standard CR / new-project flow in the Project Workbench. Person, project, and CC names are never exposed.

sections.title: Workbench → Check Availability slide-over (v5.2 W6, §13.9)
sections.body: Project Leads working in the Project Workbench's Forecast & Planning tab can open the role-availability grid as a **50%-viewport slide-over** without leaving the project. A new **Check availability** button sits in the F&P actions cluster (next to Rolling Forecast Review); clicking it opens a wide right-side drawer with the same scope controls + KPI summary + grid + role detail panel as the standalone `/capacity/availability` page, in slide-over rendering mode. Selecting a slot's **Request this role** button closes the drawer and populates a banner above the F&P grid with the captured role / location / suggested period (the suggested month is the one with highest `available_hours` across the visible window). The banner has Edit / Clear (×) controls; selecting Edit re-opens the drawer with the prior context. The standalone `/capacity/availability` page is unchanged — it still uses the page header and the shared 280px side panel.
